title: I'm building an Elder-Scrolls style RPG using Components to scale
author: Salty_Possible155
selftext:
Hey all. So I've been working on this Elder Scrolls style RPG for the past few weeks called Valenfeld. I'm making it on spawn (more AI friendly). 

  
I have a *ton* of work to do but it's been a great experience so far. I've got most of the basic systems like crafting, talents, spells and combat online, though they need a lot of polish still.

  
The graphics aren't great (yet) because most of the work I've been doing is behind the scenes. 

I've been working on a way to generate the whole world as a function, like procedural generation, but with the ability to hand-author things as well. I'm doing this through literally building JSX components (since I'm using a web stack.) It's actually working great! So I can build a component for a town which specifies all of the different buildings and such in the town, then I can inject the context of a certain architectural style and it will change the building styles. 

  
A world as large as the one I'm trying to build could not realistically be authored by one person without procedural generation and a ton of code abstraction. It's very difficult to keep the AI on the rails of not hand-placing things but it's starting to work out. I have a few types of dungeons, interiors, architectural styles, and outdoor biomes. 

Today I've just started to work with critic loops to improve the graphics. I'm really just getting started. We'll see how far I can push the realism within my token budget.

  
It's been great working on Spawn. They're a very AI friendly gamer community and I think it will grow. I dont ever plan on launching on Steam, I kind of see this as the new wave that AI game dev is taking away from steam. I'll keep you guys in the loop with updates and learnings. I have a long ways to go, but my goal is to build a game with actual depth, that's 100% authored by AI (the horror!)

  
[https://www.spawn.co/@chubigans/valenfeld](https://www.spawn.co/@chubigans/valenfeld)

comments.author: dilberry
comments.body: The grips for weapons are such a pain eh? I think my Claude crew has it mostly sorted, but man is it annoying.

replies.author: Salty_Possible155
replies.body: haha i'll get to it. This is my second rodeo (first was in Godot) - and previously I spent over a month on modular armor, grips etc. So I'm putting it off behind the actual world building.

replies.author: dilberry
replies.body:
I hear that - I have a similar sort of game going. Oblivion meets Diablo meets WoW in a few different ways. 

I just got procedural Skyrim style castles, forts, keeps, and towers sorted with random seeds for the size, style, monsters or NPCs, cave system below for castles, forts, and keeps, terrain handling, walls, courtyards, outbuildings for castles, monster camps etc. Several variants of style / shape / size etc. 

Always trying to not get stuck in that overbuilding loop though where you have this huge thing with no real gameplay… right now I have about 80 different high-quality rigged and animated enemy models, 30 NPC models, 6 different guard models, 10 different armor/weapon materials, etc etc etc. 

I moved away from fully modular armor to full armor sets plus modular helmets, weapons, shields, cloaks and accessories. For me in a fully 3D game it felt like it was either going to be jank or a lot of hand modeling to get individual armor pieces to work right.

replies.author: Salty_Possible155
replies.body: yeah i know what you mean. thats why im happy to be building on a web platform for my first real release - way less temptation to overbuild!
